El Nino Watchelninowatch.so

Forecast and alert sources

Every outside service El Nino Watch uses to forecast rain and river flow, to raise alerts, and to check those alerts against what has been observed in Somalia.

Each entry says what the app uses it for.

← Back to El Nino Watch Download PDF (English) Privacy notice ↓ Checked against the app on 19 October 2026.
Official national source: Somali National Hydrological Services (MOEWR)

The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources publishes the national flood forecast the app shows as official alerts. ICPAC's regional forecasts, Google Flood Hub's river forecasts and GDACS event monitoring are not official warnings, and the app labels them that way.

Forecasts

5 sources
  • Open-Meteo Weather Forecast APIOpen-Meteo

    Daily and hourly rainfall forecasts for all 30 cities. The app's server fetches them once and shares them with every visitor. These are computer model estimates, not station measurements.

    Terms: Data under CC BY 4.0. The free API is for non-commercial use only, under 10,000 calls a day; commercial use needs a paid plan.

    • Abouthttps://open-meteo.com/en/docs
    • APIhttps://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast
    • Termshttps://open-meteo.com/en/terms
  • Open-Meteo Flood APIGloFAS river discharge, via Open-Meteo

    River discharge forecast for each city.

    Terms: GloFAS data from the Copernicus Emergency Management Service: free, full and open access with the source credited, and no warranty. Open-Meteo’s terms above also apply.

    • Abouthttps://open-meteo.com/en/docs/flood-api
    • APIhttps://flood-api.open-meteo.com/v1/flood
    • Termshttps://ewds.climate.copernicus.eu/licences/cems-floods
  • ICPAC Weekly Exceptional Rainfall ForecastAlso alertsIGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre

    Heavy, very heavy and extremely heavy rainfall forecasts for the week (above the 90th, 95th and 99th percentiles for that week of the year). Drives the Alerts tab and the rainfall layers on the flood map.

    Terms: ICPAC does not state a reuse licence for these products. It takes data requests through its data request page.

    • Abouthttps://www.icpac.net/weekly-forecast/
    • Portalhttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/
    • Datahttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/api/datasets/
    • Map layershttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/mapserver/
    • Termshttps://www.icpac.net/data-request/
  • ENSO Diagnostic DiscussionNOAA Climate Prediction Center

    The current El Niño status and outlook.

    Terms: No licence is stated on the CPC page. NOAA treats information on its servers as public domain unless marked otherwise, and asks to be credited.

    • Abouthttps://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_advisory/ensodisc.shtml
    • Termshttps://gml.noaa.gov/about/disclaimer.html
  • Weekly Niño sea-surface temperature indexNOAA Climate Prediction Center

    Weekly El Niño ocean temperatures.

    Terms: No licence is stated on the CPC page. NOAA treats information on its servers as public domain unless marked otherwise, and asks to be credited.

    • Datahttps://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/wksst9120.for

Alerts and event monitoring

4 sources
  • Somali National Hydrological ServicesOfficialMinistry of Energy and Water Resources (MOEWR)

    The official national flood forecast: each region's daily flood level (advisory, watch or warning) for the active rainy season, with anticipatory-action pre-activation and activation. Shown as official alerts for the cities in each region.

    Terms: Used with the Ministry’s permission.

    • Portalhttps://hydro.tekhub.so/
  • Google Flood HubGoogle Research · Flood Forecasting API

    River flood forecasts at river gauges, from Google's AI model. A gauge forecast at Flood Hub's Warning, Danger or Extreme level within 25 km of a monitored city becomes an alert for that city. A model forecast, not an official warning. Used once Google approves the app's access to the API; the data is under the CC BY 4.0 licence.

    Terms: Data under CC BY 4.0.

    • Portalhttps://sites.research.google/floods/
    • APIhttps://floodforecasting.googleapis.com/v1/
    • Guidehttps://developers.google.com/flood-forecasting
  • GDACSGlobal Disaster Alert and Coordination System

    Flood and other disaster events affecting Somalia, shown as event monitoring.

    Terms: Provided as is, without warranty; GDACS says its information is purely indicative and not for decision-making. No reuse licence is stated.

    • Abouthttps://www.gdacs.org/
    • APIhttps://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventlist/SEARCH
    • Guidehttps://gdacs.org/Documents/2025/GDACS_API_quickstart_v1.pdf
    • Termshttps://gdacs.org/About/termofuse.aspx
  • ICPAC Weekly Exceptional Rainfall ForecastListed under Forecasts

    Rainfall alerts for each city, from the forecast above.

    • Portalhttps://eahazardswatch.icpac.net/

Observations that support the alerts

5 sources

What has actually been measured or seen from satellites, used to check forecasts and alerts against conditions on the ground.

  • SWALIM river stationsFAO Somalia Water and Land Information Management

    Observed river levels on the Juba and Shabelle, compared with flood thresholds.

    Terms: SWALIM does not state a reuse licence: most records in its data catalogue list none. Ask FAO SWALIM before reusing the data elsewhere.

    • Stationshttps://snrfa.faoswalim.org/stations/
    • FRRIMShttps://frrims.faoswalim.org/

    Flood extent mapped from Sentinel-1 radar.

    Terms: Copernicus Emergency Management Service terms: free and open access, commercial use included, with the service credited and no warranty.

Audio bulletin

Somali and English

A short spoken bulletin at 06:30, 12:30 and 18:30 East Africa Time, in Somali and English, first on the home page. It is written by a fixed template from the sources on this page and read by a computer voice (Google Gemini). It is not an official warning: official flood warnings come only from MOEWR.

  • El Nino Watch audio bulletinAudioEl Nino Watch · read by Google Gemini (voice Puck)

    Built from MOEWR's official flood levels, SWALIM's Juba and Shabelle river gauges, Open-Meteo's rain forecast for the 30 cities, ICPAC's weekly heavy-rain outlook, NOAA's El Niño status and news items in the bulletin's own language, with the source named. Nothing is machine-translated. The last seven days of bulletins are kept, and each can be saved as MP3.

    • Listenelninowatch.so/#podcast
    • RSS, Somalihttps://elninowatch.so/podcast.xml
    • RSS, Englishhttps://elninowatch.so/podcast-en.xml

Public health guidance

10 sources

The public health alert and the films on the Diseases tab are based on these World Health Organization documents. They are guidance, not outbreak reports.

  • Diseases from dirty waterFilmEl Nino Watch film · English, with Somali captions

    A narrated overview of cholera, dysentery, typhoid and hepatitis A and E: how they spread, how to prevent them and when to get help. It is based on the WHO fact sheets in this list.

    • Filmelninowatch.so/#waterborne-film
  • Cholera: protect your familyFilmEl Nino Watch film · English and Somali

    A narrated film on preventing cholera: safe water, handwashing, latrines, safe food and ORS. It plays in the reader's language and is based on the WHO cholera fact sheet and WHO's floods guidance below.

    • Filmelninowatch.so/#health-film
  • Malaria: protect your familyFilmEl Nino Watch film · English; Somali coming

    A narrated film on preventing malaria: treated bed nets, removing standing water, stopping bites, and testing a fever the same day. It is based on the WHO malaria fact sheet and WHO's floods guidance below.

    • Filmelninowatch.so/#malaria-film
  • Dysentery and typhoid: protect your familyFilmEl Nino Watch film · English; Somali coming

    A narrated film on dysentery and typhoid: the signs of each, safe water, handwashing, safe food, latrines, ORS, and medicine only from a health worker. It is based on the WHO typhoid and diarrhoeal disease fact sheets and WHO's floods guidance below.

    • Filmelninowatch.so/#dysentery-film
  • Hepatitis A and E: protect your familyFilmEl Nino Watch film · English; Somali coming

    A narrated film on hepatitis A and E: the signs, why hepatitis E is dangerous in pregnancy, safe water, handwashing, latrines, safe food, and seeing a health worker. It is based on the WHO hepatitis A and E fact sheets and WHO's floods guidance below.

    • Filmelninowatch.so/#hepatitis-film
  • Global Public Health Situation Analysis, El Niño 2026World Health Organization (WHO)

    Lists cholera and other waterborne disease, dengue, malaria and Rift Valley fever as high or very high risks for Somalia (printed page 14).

    • Reporthttps://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/meeting-reports/global-public-health-situation-analysis-el-nino-2026_.pdf
  • Somalia Health Emergency Appeal 2025World Health Organization (WHO)

    Describes cholera in Somalia, and malaria and dengue spreading to new districts as a direct result of flooding.

    • Appealhttps://www.who.int/publications/m/item/somalia--who-health-emergency-appeal-2025
  • Floods: how to protect your healthWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Explains contaminated drinking water, mosquitoes after floods, and preventing cholera, typhoid and malaria.

    • Q&Ahttps://www.who.int/news-room/q-a-detail/how-do-i-protect-my-health-in-a-flood
  • Water, sanitation and health in humanitarian emergenciesWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Covers infections linked to poor sanitation: diarrhoeal diseases, dysentery, hepatitis A and E, and skin infections.

    • Pagehttps://www.who.int/teams/environment-climate-change-and-health/water-sanitation-and-health/environmental-health-in-emergencies/humanitarian-emergencies
  • Rift Valley feverWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Links outbreaks in East Africa to El Niño heavy rainfall, and explains infection from livestock and mosquitoes and how to prevent it.

    • Fact sheethttps://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rift-valley-fever
  • CholeraWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Explains contaminated food and water, rapid dehydration, ORS treatment, sanitation and vaccination.

    • Fact sheethttps://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/cholera
  • Diarrhoeal diseaseWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Explains how diarrhoea spreads through contaminated food and water, that bloody diarrhoea is dysentery, and treatment with ORS and zinc, with continued feeding and breastfeeding.

    • Fact sheethttps://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/diarrhoeal-disease
  • TyphoidWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Explains that typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water, causes a prolonged high fever, is treated with antibiotics and can be prevented by vaccination.

    • Fact sheethttps://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/typhoid
  • Hepatitis AWorld Health Organization (WHO)

    Explains how hepatitis A spreads through contaminated food and water, its signs, including yellow eyes and skin and dark urine, and the vaccine.

  • Hepatitis EWorld Health Organization (WHO)

Privacy

What El Nino Watch keeps about you, and who else sees what. There are no accounts, no cookies and no advertising, and nothing is sold.

  • Visit counts

    Each page load is counted, with the tab, city, language, type of device and the country the connection comes from, and so is each play of the audio bulletin. No cookies, internet addresses or browser details are stored, and browsers that ask not to be tracked are not counted. The totals are shown on the visitor statistics page.

  • Community reports

    Reports and comments are public: what you write, the name or alias you give (or Anonymous), any location you add, and photos or videos exactly as uploaded, which may contain location data. Your internet address is held in memory for up to 10 minutes to limit abuse, and is never saved. Only the browser that sent a report can delete it, using a receipt kept in that browser.

  • WhatsApp alerts

    If you sign up, your WhatsApp number, the cities you follow, your language and whether you asked for the audio bulletin are kept only to send those messages. Messages go through Meta's WhatsApp service. Replying STOP deletes them.

  • Saved in your browser

    Your language, home city, added cities, report receipts, alerts already shown, city manager review stages and private notes are saved in your own browser, not sent to El Nino Watch. Clearing the site's data in your browser removes them.

  • Other services

    Forecasts, alerts and news are fetched by the El Nino Watch server, so those services do not see you. The audio bulletins are written from those sources and voiced by Google's Gemini service; nothing about you is sent to it. The flood map's background (OpenStreetMap or Esri), its layers and the place-name search for added cities load directly from their publishers, who see your internet address as any website does. Share buttons contact X or Facebook only when you tap them. The site is hosted on bunny.net, which handles every request as any web host does.

Questions about privacy: contact@mandekconsulting.com

Not listed: the base map and elevation services (Natural Earth, OpenStreetMap, Esri World Imagery, Open-Meteo Elevation and place-name search), which draw the map but do not forecast or alert.

Map backgrounds: Natural Earth is in the public domain. OpenStreetMap data are © OpenStreetMap contributors under the Open Database License, and its map tiles are used under the OpenStreetMap Foundation’s tile usage policy. Esri World Imagery is used under Esri’s terms.

Community reports in the app come from residents and are unverified.
